project.name: Fantasy
project.identity: A local-first dynasty fantasy football intelligence product for format-aware team decisions.
project.audience: Dynasty fantasy managers who need evidence-backed decisions for their specific league and roster.
project.core_loop: Ingest league, market, player, and prospect data, model the team's context, rank actionable paths, inspect evidence and freshness, then make a manual roster, trade, waiver, or draft decision.
project.north_star: A manager can state what their team is, what its best path is, who to trade with, what deal to make, and whether a prospect or pick decision is sharp in that format and league.
not_this: An opaque answer built on stale or untraceable data

mvp.definition: One league can be ingested into a Command Center that explains actionable team decisions with visible data freshness and degraded-source boundaries.

complete_product.definition: Multi-league intelligence covers trades, waivers, rookies, weekly decisions, and portfolio management with reproducible refreshes and evidence-backed recommendations.

outcomes.name: The product identifies a manager's roster state and ranks format-aware paths for trades, waivers, and prospect or pick decisions.

layers.intended: Managers receive sharp, league-specific paths rather than generic rankings.
layers.planned: The planning state centres the Command Center and Edge Radar around actionable decisions.
layers.implemented: The local FastAPI, React, DuckDB, and player intelligence surfaces provide partial decision support.
layers.verified: Repository planning and current surfaces establish partial implementation; this bootstrap did not rerun the engine or endpoint verification.

evidence.note: Describes the local-first dynasty fantasy football intelligence product and stack.
States the core value as explaining team state, best path, trade partner, deal, and prospect or pick sharpness.

blockers.summary: Current dense-source readiness, refresh behavior, and recommendation quality still need bounded execution evidence.

outcomes.name: Every actionable output makes its source coverage, freshness, and degraded readiness visible enough for a manager to judge it.

layers.intended: No consequential fantasy decision should look more certain than its underlying data.
layers.planned: The project tracks dense metadata, source readiness, and degraded versus dense-source operation.
layers.implemented: Source and metadata pathways exist in the current engine and Edge Radar work.
layers.verified: The repository records readiness work, but end-to-end freshness and provenance are not reverified here.

evidence.note: Records the current Edge Radar focus and distinction between degraded and dense-source readiness.

blockers.summary: Source coverage and write/read concurrency boundaries still constrain reproducible refresh evidence.

drift.summary: The intended decision product is broader than any single current Edge Radar or Command Center slice, and end-to-end recommendation quality remains unverified.
